mode: Edit selected Codex: GitHub-inspired style with physical control depth
prompt:
Use case: style-transfer / ui-mockup.
Edit image 1, the existing Copilot Hub Tower Codex screen, with a distinctly GitHub-inspired visual style. Produce one finished full-screen landscape 16:9 game mock-up, crisp and readable. Keep this a low-poly game's interactive Lab station with a live 3D character, not a browser, repository page or SaaS dashboard.

INPUT ROLES: image 1 is the edit target and exact composition/content authority. Image 2 is the real Hub world reference; keep its low-poly architecture, trees, neutral daylight and restrained mood. Image 3 is the canonical Developer character, whose geometry and colors must not change.

ART DIRECTION — GITHUB PRODUCT LANGUAGE APPLIED TO PHYSICAL GAME UI:
Take inspiration from GitHub's Primer visual language: near-black charcoal and graphite neutrals, precise quiet borders, clear compact sans-serif typography, small simple line icons like Octicons, restrained familiar green selection accents, small radii and meticulous alignment. Art-direction palette: charcoal near #0d1117, inset graphite near #161b22, raised dark-gray near #21262d, soft gray borders near #30363d, light text near #e6edf3, muted text near #8b949e, green near #238636 with a brighter small green indicator. These colors guide the image, not displayed text.
Make the visual shift substantial and coherent. Replace the blue UI panel surfaces with graphite/charcoal, simplify the decorative typography, reduce rainbow saturation in the stats, and bring the selection controls into this darker GitHub palette. Retain the ivory physical Lab shell and blue-gray room/window architecture so the screen still belongs to the surrounding Hub. Do not darken the whole scene or turn it into a night scene.

PHYSICAL DEPTH MUST SURVIVE:
The last revision fixed flat buttons; preserve this improvement. Make the animation keys shorter and more precise than the bulky ivory keycaps, with graphite top faces, fine light edge definition, visible dark sidewalls, small planar bevels and contact shadows. They remain tangible raised controls in one recessed charcoal console, not flat HTML button rectangles. Idle alone is a pressed green key with a small green status light; use white text and icon on it. All other keys are neutral graphite with light-gray labels. The selected key sits slightly lower in its socket.
There are EXACTLY SEVEN keys, EXACTLY SEVEN sockets, evenly spaced, labelled in order: "Rest", "Idle", "Work", "Move", "Place", "Hit", "Resolve". No extra blank key. Use compact understated monochrome line pictograms rather than oversized cartoon icons. Place the label "Animations" above the row.
Back to Hub and camera Reset become secondary graphite controls with thin borders, subtle bevels and a visible lower lip. They belong to the same control family. Keep Back to Hub top right and Reset next to the model. Do not add any new controls.

ROSTER, STATS AND TYPE:
Preserve the physical noticeboard silhouette and off-white cap at left. Refinish its inset backing to charcoal. Portrait dossiers become neatly mounted thin graphite plaques with quiet gray borders, consistent rounded corners and visible thickness. Retain the character portraits and current seven-card arrangement. Selected Developer has a fine green edge and modest green selection marker instead of cyan neon bloom. Keep all names exactly: "Base", "Developer", "Tester", "Analyst", "Security", "Architect", "Linter".
Keep the central Developer preview dominant on its ivory-backed physical plinth. Header "Developer" in a clean compact semibold GitHub-like sans serif, subtitle "Direct-output specialist" in subdued gray. Make metadata/breadcrumb lettering gently monospaced, not the whole UI.
Right stats panel is matte charcoal in the existing ivory equipment shell. Header "Stats". Use crisp thin monochrome icons, subdued dividers and segmented meter rows made of small rounded square cells reminiscent of GitHub's restrained contribution squares. Use a unified calm green for filled cells, dark graphite for unfilled; separate the Compute row subtly. This is a visual game capability readout, NOT an activity calendar. Exact labels: "Damage", "Work", "Action speed", "Range", "Compute". Keep Damage below halfway, Work full, Action speed full, Range around two-thirds, Compute mostly filled. No numbers, units, percentages, prices, totals, chart-axis labels or rankings anywhere.
Preserve the game's COPILOT / TOWER DEFENSE identity and use the breadcrumb "Copilot Hub / Tower Codex". No added GitHub wordmark, Octocat mascot, repository navigation, commits, pull requests, source code, contribution-calendar dates or browser chrome. The GitHub influence comes from the materials, controls, icons, colors and type.

INVARIANTS:
Animation SELECTION ONLY: no playback-speed control, play/pause, timeline, scrubber, replay button or loop switch. Reset is strictly the camera control. Retain orbit arrows and "Drag to rotate · Tilt · Zoom".
Keep the existing scene layout, bright daylight through the windows, low-poly park and campus setting, model scale, camera angle and simple matte materials. No duplicate Lab building outside the window. No photoreal materials, metallic machinery, film grain, dramatic glow or cinematic depth of field.
Developer remains the canonical floating HEAD ONLY, faceted orange swept spikes, dark goggles, teal lenses, black face with exactly two cyan eyes, cream ear pieces with curly-brace glyph. Do not recolor or redesign the character. No extra props or characters.
The result should feel like a GitHub-designed control console physically built into this exact Copilot Hub game world.
